questions.q: Which of the following data structures is used in recursion?
questions.e: Each function call is pushed onto the call stack and popped when it returns, so recursion uses a stack.

questions.q: Which sorting algorithm has the worst-case time complexity of O(n²) but performs well for small datasets?
questions.e: Bubble Sort compares neighbours again and again, so its worst case is O(n²), but it is simple and fine for tiny lists.

questions.q: Which data structure is used in Breadth-First Search (BFS)?
questions.e: BFS visits nodes level by level, so it uses a queue.

questions.q: Which data structure is best for implementing a LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) system?
questions.e: A stack is last in, first out.

questions.q: Which algorithm is commonly used for shortest path problems in graphs?
questions.e: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest paths from a start node in a weighted graph.

questions.q: Which data structure is used for implementing recursion?
questions.e: A stack stores the return points of function calls.

questions.q: What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?
questions.e: Binary search halves the search range each step, so it takes O(log n).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a property of a heap data structure?
o: All levels except possibly the last are fully filled
Parent nodes are greater or lesser than their child nodes
Elements are stored in sorted order
questions.e: A heap is a complete binary tree ordered between parent and child, but it is not fully sorted.

questions.q: What is the best-case time complexity of Quick Sort?
questions.e: Quick sort's best case is O(n log n), when the pivot splits the list evenly.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of a doubly linked list over a singly linked list?
questions.e: A doubly linked list has links in both directions, so you can move forward and backward.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of operations for evaluating an expression in postfix notation?
questions.e: A postfix (reverse Polish) expression is evaluated from left to right using a stack.

questions.q: Which type of tree is balanced by keeping the heights of subtrees within a certain limit?
questions.e: An AVL tree keeps the heights of its two subtrees within 1 of each other.

questions.q: What is the worst-case time complexity of insertion sort?
questions.e: Insertion sort's worst case, a reverse-sorted list, is O(n²).

questions.q: Which data structure follows the First In, First Out (FIFO) principle?
questions.e: A queue is first in, first out.

questions.q: In computer graphics, what does GPU stand for?
questions.e: GPU stands for Graphics Processing Unit.

questions.q: Which data structure uses a Last In, First Out (LIFO) approach?
questions.e: A stack is last in, first out.

questions.q: Which data structure organizes data in a hierarchy with a top-down, tree-like structure?
questions.e: A tree arranges data in a hierarchy.
